chunks: Turn uprightly to God without ascribing compeers to Him; for he who associates any one with God is like a thing that falls from the sky and is either snatched away by birds or carried far away by the wind.

key_terms.حُنَفَاءَ: Upright monotheists, followers of the pure faith of Abraham
key_terms.مُشْرِكِينَ: Those who associate partners with God (polytheists)

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of being Hanifa and the metaphor of falling from the sky in Surah Al-Hajj?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse from Surah Al-Hajj is often linked to the concept of *Fitrah* (innate monotheism), urging believers to return to the pure, unadulterated worship of Allah as established by the Prophet Muhammad. The vivid metaphor of the sky-faller illustrates the spiritual disorientation and ultimate loss of direction experienced by those who introduce *Shirk* into their faith, contrasting it with the stability of true monotheism.
